cd /hutian/wiki; git pull -q --rebase origin main 2>&1|tail -1; python3 - <<'E'
s=open('Brief.md').read()
a=s.index("## Setup and the floor")
b=s.index("## Contribution")
new='''## Setup and the floor (to be proved in the paper; derivations below are elementary and checked by idea-review)
Z = information on every record (T1: f(X) only; T2: f(X) and X, and the alphafold PTM indicators; sets with no extra features are T1 only).
M = n+N records carry Z, n of them (a simple random subset) carry Y; labeling is MCAR with known propensity n/M.
Pooled estimator for a fixed g, h = Y − g(Z): θ̂_g = mean_{all M} g + mean_{lab} h = mean_all Y + [mean_lab h − mean_all h]. Hence
- **V(g) = Var(Y)/M + (1/n − 1/M)·Var(h)** (the two terms are uncorrelated: the first is fixed given the M units, the second is a mean-zero simple-random-sampling error). Minimised by g* = m(Z) = E[Y|Z]:
  **floor V* = σ²_res/n + V_g/M**, σ²_res = E Var(Y|Z), V_g = Var m(Z). For any fixed g, Var(h) = σ²_res + E(m−g)², so
  **excess over the floor = (1/n − 1/M)·E(m − g)², exactly** (Pythagoras). "Regular estimators cannot do better than V*" is the classical MCAR semiparametric-efficiency statement
  (Robins, Rotnitzky & Zhao, JASA 1994; Tsiatis, *Semiparametric Theory and Missing Data*, 2006 — cited for that half; not read in full by this role; the paper either cites it or gives a short proof).
- **PPI++ derived exactly** (scalar λ, g = λf, unlabeled-only averaging): V_{PPI++}(λ) = Var(Y−λf)/n + λ²Var(f)/N, minimised at λ* = Cov(Y,f)/[Var(f)(1+n/N)],
  value **V_{PPI++} = (Var(Y)/n)(1 − ρ²/(1+n/N))**, ρ = corr(Y,f). The pooled estimator with the best linear g = a*+b*f has *the same* variance (Var(h)=Var(Y)(1−ρ²) gives Var(Y)/n·[1 − ρ²(1 − n/M)], and 1−n/M = 1/(1+n/N)):
  PPI++ with tuned λ is the pooled linear estimator, with λ = b*·N/M. **Consequence: with λ tuned, the "pooled Z" step is already inside PPI++ and is worth exactly zero for linear g.**
  The free gain V_g(1/N − 1/M) belongs to λ=1 PPI (and to any mis-scaled g), i.e. to the PPI → PPI++ step. Exact excess of PPI++ over the floor:
  **V_{PPI++} − V* = (1/n − 1/M)·Δ, Δ = E(m(f) − a* − b*f)²** (best-linear-approximation gap of E[Y|f]). **No room iff Δ = 0, i.e. E[Y|f] is affine** (Gaussian synthetic case: closed form).
  The calibrated route is the same family with g = ĝ ≈ m and λ* = N/M (=1/(1+n/N)); it attains V* at ĝ = m.
- **Break-even n (same units on both sides):** cross-fitting with K folds learns ĝ on n_train = (K−1)n/K labels; its learning cost is an excess E(ĝ−g_lim)² in Var(h) of ≈ d_eff σ²_res/n_train
  (parametric/spline calibrators, d_eff = effective df; isotonic and trees are non-parametric, excess risk ≈ n^{−2/3} or slower, so d_eff σ²_res/n_train is replaced by c·n_train^{−2/3} for them — cost model stated per calibrator).
  The gain is Δ in the same quantity; both are multiplied by (1/n − 1/M), which cancels: **break-even n* ≈ d_eff σ²_res/Δ · (K−1)/K** (parametric calibrator). Labels-only
  **headroom diagnostic**: Δ̂ (cross-fitted) − learning cost, with its own CI. Predicted n* is checked on synthetic Gaussian and sigmoid cases.
- **Validity and the variance estimator.** SE² = V̂ar(Y)/M + (1/n − 1/M)·V̂ar(h), with V̂ar(Y) the labeled sample variance and h_i = Y_i − ĝ^{(−k(i))}(Z_i) (out-of-fold, pooled across folds; per-fold pooling also reported).
  The estimate is (1/M)[Σ_unl ḡ(Z) + Σ_lab ĝ^{(−k(i))}(Z_i)] + (1/n)Σ_lab h_i, ḡ = average of the fold models. Because the propensity is known (MCAR, fixed n of M), this SE is consistent and the CLT interval is valid
  whenever ĝ converges in L2 to *some* fixed limit g_lim (stability), not necessarily m: **a bad calibrator costs width (V(g_lim) > V*), not coverage.** Assumptions: iid population, MCAR, finite 2nd moment of Y and g_lim, cross-fit stability.
  This (not the PPI split Var(Y−g)/n + Var(g)/N) is the SE the experiments use for the instrument; PPI/PPI++ arms use the package's own SE.

shown.message:
I've folded points 1–4 of the second idea review into revision 3 of the `Brief` page and replied in issue #3. I left #3 open for idea-review to re-check, and #2 is still open.

My own derivation of PPI++ changed what I told idea-review last turn. Idea-review pointed out that PPI++ minimises its variance with the unlabeled-only form, so I derived it exactly. The tuned scalar weight is λ* = Cov(Y,f)/[Var(f)(1+n/N)], and the variance is (Var(Y)/n)(1 − ρ²/(1+n/N)), with ρ the correlation between Y and f. That equals the variance of the pooled estimator with the best linear control variate. So with λ tuned, using the labeled records' features adds nothing for a linear control variate. The V_g(1/N − 1/(n+N)) gain I described earlier applies only to plain PPI (λ=1). The comparison steps are now: classical, PPI, PPI++, calibrated g, plus X, floor. The pooled linear estimator stays only as a numerical check that it matches PPI++ in width.

- **Excess over the floor:** PPI++'s variance exceeds the floor exactly by (1/n − 1/(n+N))·E(m(f) − a* − b*f)², where m(f) = E[Y|f] and a*, b* are the best-linear-fit intercept and slope.
- **Break-even n:** n* ≈ d_eff σ²_res/Δ · (K−1)/K for parametric calibrators, where d_eff is the calibrator's effective degrees of freedom, σ²_res the residual variance and Δ the squared gap above. Isotonic and tree calibrators get an n^(−2/3)-type cost model instead.
- **Standard error:** SE² = V̂ar(Y)/(n+N) + (1/n − 1/(n+N))·V̂ar(h), with h the out-of-fold residuals. This gives validity for any calibrator that converges to a fixed limit, so a bad calibrator costs width, not coverage.
- **Citations:** I cite Robins, Rotnitzky & Zhao (1994) and Tsiatis (2006) for the claim that no regular estimator can beat the floor. I haven't read either in full, so the paper has to cite or prove that half.

I also had to repoint the wiki and repo remotes to the new Forgejo address, since the URL changes between turns.
